Russia.text: The Russian Empire, proclaimed in 1721, became the third-largest empire in history.
Russia.evidence: It was proclaimed as the Russian Empire in 1721, which became the third-largest empire in history.

Canada.text: It has the longest coastline of any country, and its border with the US is the longest land border.
Canada.evidence: making it the second-largest country by total area, with the longest coastline of any country. Its border with the United States is the longest international land border.

China.text: Unified under the Qin in 221 BCE, beginning two millennia of imperial rule.
China.evidence: In 221 BCE, China was unified under the Qin, followed by the Han dynasty, ushering in two millennia of imperial rule across periods of unity and division.

United States.text: Beyond its 50 states, it claims five major island territories in Oceania and the Caribbean.
United States.evidence: The United States also asserts sovereignty over five major island territories and various uninhabited islands in Oceania and the Caribbean.

Brazil.text: Covering roughly half of South America, it borders every country on the continent except Ecuador and Chile.
Brazil.evidence: Covering roughly half of South America's land area, it borders all other countries and territories on the continent except Ecuador and Chile.

Australia.text: It sits on the world's flattest and driest inhabited continent.
Australia.evidence: It has a land area of 7,688,287 km2 (2,968,464 sq mi), making it the sixth-largest country in the world, and is the world's flattest and driest inhabited continent.

India.text: Its Middle kingdoms carried Dravidian scripts and traditions to Southeast Asia in the first millennium CE.
India.evidence: In South India, across the first millennium CE, the Middle kingdoms transmitted Dravidian language scripts and cultural traditions to Southeast Asia.

Argentina.text: It claims sovereignty over the Falkland Islands and a part of Antarctica.
Argentina.evidence: Argentina claims sovereignty over the Falkland Islands, South Georgia and the South Sandwich Islands, the Southern Patagonian Ice Field, and a part of Antarctica.

Kazakhstan.text: The largest landlocked country in the world, yet it has a coastline along the Caspian Sea.
Kazakhstan.evidence: Kazakhstan, officially the Republic of Kazakhstan, is a landlocked country situated primarily in Central Asia, ... and it has a coastline along the Caspian Sea. ... Kazakhstan is the world's ninth-largest country by land area and the largest landlocked country.

Algeria.text: France annexed it in 1848 but did not fully conquer it until 1903.
Algeria.evidence: After nearly three centuries as a major power in the Mediterranean, the country was invaded by France in 1830 and formally annexed in 1848, though it was not fully conquered and pacified until 1903.
